Posted December 13, 2001
(MarijuanaNews note: When discussing many issues, Canadians generally tend to look over their shoulders in a southerly direction and wonder what their superpower neighbor will think about the subject.

This is especially true of my friends in the Canadian marijuana reform movement.

They know all too well that DEAland is the Vatican, the Kremlin, of reefer madness and leans hard on countries to toe the prohibitionist party line, even when a change in cannabis policies could have no direct impact on it.

They are also very aware that ending marijuana prohibition in Canada would make it very difficult to maintain the war on cannabis in DEAland. So, as Canada moves tentatively away from cannabis prohibition, they have been waiting for the other jackboot to drop.

Whatever may be going on behind the scenes, what has happened publicly is a bit unexpected. In fact, it is down right bizarre. Wealthy Vancouverites, Lynda and Robert Bentall, the retired chairman of the Bentall Corporation, have formed something called the International Drug Education and Awareness Society (IDEAS, they call it, but everyone here sees it as iDEAs.

The Bentalls, who seem to be the ultimate prohibitionist true believers, are sponsoring a reefer madness summit in Vancouver, of all places, the first week in May, of all times. And they have announced the " symposium " in a series of ads in the Vancouver papers, attacking medical marijuana, of all things.

They are putting up C$200,000 (about US$130,000) to fund the conference which will be a lovely junket for narks and related prohibition industry workers.

To make things even weirder, they have allied themselves not only with the usual crackpots, like Dr. Eric Voth,

and the Swedish prohibitionists at the Hassela Nordic Network,

In what business lawyers would call a failure of " due diligence, " the Bentalls have gotten into bed the Semblers of Florida, of the Drug Free America Foundation, the pathetic prohibitionist propaganda pushers, and the notorious Straight Inc., the rehab racket that has paid out huge sums to settle cases of abusive " treatment. "

It is ironic that Mrs. Bentall, who devotes herself to trying to help troubled youth, would partner with people who have done so much harm to young people.

Perhaps they were deceived by the Semblers’ political prominence. Mel Sembler is a big wheel in the Republican Party, former US Ambassador to Australia, and is now nominated to be Bush’s ambassador to Italy.

Probably with input from some of their new friends, the Bentalls are running three ads in Canadian papers to promote the conference and to promulgate their iDEAs. One of the ads deals with needle exchange, and that is too far off topic for me, but the other two deal with medical marijuana and the supposed success of Sweden’s prohibitionist policies, topics with which I am all too familiar.

What follows is my critique of those two ads -- and an article in a Vancouver weekly, that shows that Mrs. Bentall is abysmally ignorant of the literature, which makes her very useful to her new DEAland partners.

The text of the ads and the Vancouver Courier article is in italics. All emphasis is added.)

International Drug Education & Awareness Symposium

‘MEDICAL ’ MARIJUANA KILLS LIKE TOBACCO

(MarijuanaNews note: The wonderful thing about this ad is that a lot of it is wrong, but all of it is irrelevant. However, I will deal with the factual points anyway, out of habit, I suppose.)

The Facts Are Clear...the issue of Marijuana has become politically motivated pseudoscience...

• Marijuana has grown more potent over the decades.

(MarijuanaNews note: Largely wrong, and entirely irrelevant. The more potent the cannabis, the better it is for medical purposes.)

A joint now contains about three times the tar of a cigarette, plus known cancer-causing carcinogens such as vinyl chloride, dimethynitrosamine, methylethynitrosamine, benz(a)anthracene, benzo(a)pyrene, as well as carbon dioxide, ammonia and more than 20 other major toxins.

(SOURCE: UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA AT LOS ANGELES AND NEW ENGLAND JOURNAL OF MEDICINE)

(MarijuanaNews note: Ironically, the ad began by saying that " the issue of Marijuana has become politically motivated pseudoscience... " but from here on the ad is completely political, and one long non sequitur. Medical marijuana is dangerous because of the alleged motives of its supporters, the " pro-dope movement. " Allowing the medical use of a substance creates popular support for allowing its non-medical use, except for morphine, barbiturates, benzodiazapenes, etc., etc.)

• Consider that when Alaska briefly legalized pot, the use of marijuana and cocaine among adolescents soared more than twice that of any other U.S. state.

And, Alaska did not briefly " legalize pot. " A state supreme court ruling, still in effect in some – perhaps all -- of the state, allows people to have it in their homes. Until recently, there was no good data allowing comparisons of various states’ usage levels, by adolescents or adults. At present, it appears that Colorado may have the highest rate of marijuana use. Teen cocaine use is so low that comparing state data is meaningless, if not impossible. Moreover, this proves nothing about anything, especially medical marijuana.)

In Holland where dope smoking is permitted, use among 11 to 18 year olds increased 142% from 1990 to 1995;

(MarijuanaNews note: A fascinating choice of numbers to take out of context. First, there is later data available, so why did they stop at 1995? Perhaps, because teen marijuana use in Holland has gone down since then!

And large percentage increases from low numbers look impressive, if you don’t know that Dutch marijuana use at all age levels is well below that of DEAland. Below are some numbers that the Bentalls seem to have overlooked.

(MarijuanaNews note: First, comparing international crime data is very difficult, and I am dubious about these numbers,
See
The DEAland Crime Rate May Be Three Times Higher Than Is Reported

but inasmuch as marijuana use is lower in The Netherlands than it is in DEAland, then why is its de facto legality responsible for a higher rate of burglary? How would that work?)

and Holland now produces 80% of the world’s ecstacy.

(SOURCE: INTERNATIONAL DRUG STRATEGY INSTITUTE)

(MarijuanaNews note: First, even if that is true, and I doubt it, what has that got to do with anything? Medical marijuana is bad because Holland does not arrest marijuana users and because it therefore produces 80% of the world’s ecstasy???)

Second, they are, in effect, citing themselves. The International Drug Strategy Institute is a subsidiary of The Drug Free America Foundation, a cosponsor of the event. It is not an independent source of data on ecstasy, or on the spelling thereof.)

• Cannabis is no better than codeine at controlling pain and because of its undesirable side effects, " It has no place in mainstream medicine " . (SOURCE: BRITISH MEDICAL JOURNAL)

Second, one of the articles does point out that " Three quarters of British doctors surveyed in 1994 wanted cannabis available on prescription, " which is not the impression that iDEAs is trying to make.

And, the same article says that " No studies have been conducted on smoked cannabis. " And these articles were NOT about cannabis, but isolated cannabinoids!)

• PET scanning of frequent-use marijuana smokers show lower blood flow in large regions of the brain, affecting motor coordination function, cognition, timing, sensory information-processing and attention. (SOURCE:NEURO REPORT 2000:4)

• Longitudinal 10-year study of offspring exposed to marijuana in utero indicated increased hyperactivity, impulsivity, inattention, delinquency and problem-externalization. (SOURCE: NEUROTOXICOLOGY & TERATOLOGY 2000:22)

(MarijuanaNews note: Again, what is the relevance of this to medical cannabis? People who are seriously ill are unlikely to be pregnant. And Thalidomide has been approved for medical use, so put this in context.)
See
Marijuana, Caffeine, Thalidomide and the Persecution of the Sick and Dying

• Smoking marijuana can cause cancer, lung damage and babies with low birth weights. (SOURCE: INSTITUTE OF MEDICINE; NATIONAL ACADEMY OF SCIENCES, 1999)

Why doesn’t iDEAs tell us about that?)

See
Executive Summary Of The IOM Report, Marijuana And Medicine: Assessing The Science Base

Special Interest Groups have been dictating policy affecting our communities long enough...The rest of Canada needs to be heard...

(MarijuanaNews note: Actually, medical cannabis is supported by an overwhelming majority of the people of Canada, and this has certainly not been because of lobbying by " special interest groups. " )

presented by

Vancouver Convention &Exhibition Centre

With the use of statistical and documented evidence, IDEAS - 2002, the first of its kind in Canada, is committed to bringing honesty to the issue of tolerance for substance abuse.

IDEAS has invited Swedish, Swiss, U.S., Canadian and other world-leading medical, legal and police experts with impeccable credentials and experience in the prevention, treatment, law enforcement and harm reduction of illicit drugs. For three days, they will meet with Canadians of influence in a conference intended to examine Canada’s permissive drug policies.

If you have been invited, please reply Early.

Second ad:

SWEDEN WINNING WAR ON DRUGS

Proponents of ‘medical’ marijuana, needle exchange programs, methadone handouts, " soft " law enforcement, legalization, and other permissive drug strategies would have you believe Canada cannot win the War on Drugs.

(MarijuanaNews note: Again, the inclusion of medical cannabis in this list is a non sequitur, but that is the least of the problems in this ad.)

Sweden proves otherwise. By choosing zero-tolerance and a drug-free society, Sweden is eradicating illicit drug use.

(MarijuanaNews note: And Sweden is eradicating illicit drug use? Oh really?

Such an increase in marijuana use by Dutch teens was cited above as proof that Dutch policies are a failure. So wouldn’t a doubling of " narcotic drugs " use by Swedish teens prove the same about Sweden’s policies? In fairness, the Swedish teen drug use rate is low, and – as I said about the Dutch numbers – getting a large percentage increase from a low base is not meaningful. However, a doubling from any level does not sound like " eradicating illicit drug use. " )

Only 2% of young adults in Sweden are likely to have smoked cannabis in the last year. In drug-permissive countries like Holland, it’s about 14%. In Australia, 33%.

In Sweden, use of heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and amphetamines is also appreciably lower.
(MarijuanaNews note: No. On the contrary. According to the European Monitoring Center on Drugs and Drug Abuse, Sweden has 3 problem drug users per thousand and The Netherlands has 2.5. Problem drug use in the EU involves mainly opiates, with the exception of Sweden, where people who inject amphetamines represent the majority of cases. Moreover, the mortality rate from drug abuse is substantially higher in Sweden than in The Netherlands, which has the lowest drug related death rate in the EU. By contrast, almost half of all drug related deaths in the EU occur in the prohibitionist United Kingdom.)

Swedish courts can order treatment;

Is that something that Canadians would accept? Is that something that the Bentalls would advocate for Canada?)

schools and municipal social services provide extensive education against drug use;

(MarijuanaNews note: In DEAland, prohibitionist propaganda, excuse me, " education against drug use " is a multibillion dollar a year industry.)

" harm reduction " and needle-exchange have NOT been adopted.

(MarijuanaNews note: These are not widespread in DEAland.)

COMPARISON - Restrictive SWEDEN to Permissive AUSTRALIA

(MarijuanaNews note: This is very strange. While the choice of Sweden may make sense from an ideological point of view, and it is certainly " restrictive, " is it really a viable model for Canada? Even if it had been as successful as they claim – and it has not -- remember Sweden has a population less than a third of Canada’s, and it is safely tucked up in the northern part of Europe. Canada is very different. In any case, it would seem that it would be much more appropriate to use DEAland as the model, if Canada really wants a " restrictive " policy, so why is there no mention of its policies, even though several of their speakers, and co-sponsors are from there?

And the description of Australia as permissive seems a bit odd, but it is even odder that the iDEAs’ own web site has an article on it that clearly contradicts this premise:

We can now expect a continued fight against drugs.

On October 28 this year the following was issued by the Prime Minister´s Office:

The Coalition Government’s highly successful Tough on Drugs strategy will be expanded over coming years.

Today, I am announcing a package of measures totalling $109 million to boost the fight against illicit drugs…. "

Does this sound like a country whose policies are " permissive? " Or is this a prohibitionist government struggling to make failed " restrictive " policies work?)

(MarijuanaNews note: " Prevalence " means having ever used, even once. It is perhaps the least meaningful number.)

(MarijuanaNews note: The Dutch " Drug-related deaths (per million pop. is only 3, almost one tenth that of the Swedes, according to the European Monitoring Center on Drugs and Drug Abuse.

Although differences in the methods of data collection probably overstate the differences, just as the comparisons of burglary data between DEAland and The Netherlands can be misleading.

Nonetheless, choosing Australia as the model for a permissive policy is both foolish and dishonest.)

Throughout the world, statistical evidence proves tolerance as a drug policy is a failure.
(MarijuanaNews note: Actually, what the " statistical evidence proves " is that there is little correlation between the severity of the laws and the problems with drugs. On the contrary.

The UK has had some of the most restrictive laws, but they also have some of the worst problems in Europe. DEAland, of course, has a very severe drug problem, and the worlds largest prison population per capita.

The Netherlands on the other hand, has a lower rate of problem hard drug use than either DEAland or Sweden.)

Wouldn’t Sweden’s model be a better choice for Canada?

(MarijuanaNews note: Would it?)

There are solutions working in the world today!

Shouldn’t Canadians benefit from this Knowledge & Experience ?

presented by International Drug Education & Awareness Society in partnership with Drug Free America Foundation Inc. and Drug Prevention Network of the Americas

May 1 to May 3,2002

Vancouver Convention &Exhibition Centre

With the use of statistical and documented evidence, IDEAS - 2002, the first of its kind in Canada, is committed to bringing honesty to the issue of tolerance for substance abuse.

IDEAS has invited Swedish, Swiss, U.S., Canadian and other world-leading medical, legal and police experts with impeccable credentials and experience in the prevention, treatment, law enforcement and harm reduction of illicit drugs. For three days, they will meet with Canadians of influence in a conference intended to examine Canada’s permissive drug policies.

If you have been invited,please reply Early.

(MarijuanaNews note: And if you think that these ads are simplistic and misleading consider the views of Mrs. Bentall.)

From the November 26th, 2001 Vancouver Courier
Bentall money going to fight drug liberalization

By Naoibh O'Connor

A prominent Vancouver woman is organizing a conference next May to challenge the country's move towards more liberal drug policies.

Lynda Bentall, whose husband Robert is the retired chairman of the Bentall Corporation, has formed a group called the International Drug Education and Awareness Society (IDEAS) to put on the symposium, for which she's willing to supply $200,000 in funding.

Bentall, who opposes the medical use of marijuana, is taking out ads in local and national papers listing the dangers of marijuana use and needle exchanges and touting the benefits of Sweden's zero-tolerance drug policy. " There's not a qualified physician that would say an AIDS patient or a cancer patient should smoke marijuana, " said Bentall, who says she's never smoked pot.

" The point is, marijuana is an intoxicant and some people like it. This is the biggest scam that has ever been brought to Canada. "

(MarijuanaNews note: Scam? That sounds familiar. The nark lies about what I said have become a basic part of prohibitionist propaganda. I am sure that Mrs. Bentall has no idea how that worked its way into the party line and her vocabulary.)

Bentall said she wants to stimulate debate because politicians appear to be moving forward on something they don't understand. " This is very much an issue that's relevant to all Canadians. Most people have not been consulted on this, " she said.

" We have a responsibility to not just sit and complain about it. "

About 3,200 delegates, including representatives from policing, educational and government agencies across the country, have been invited to attend the conference.

About 100 students from the Lower Mainland will also be selected to participate for free in the event, which normally costs $425 per person.

Experts from the United States and as far away as Sweden are expected to give presentations. They include Christy A. McCampbell, PhD, a former undercover cop and senior special agent in charge of the California Department of Justice Bureau of Narcotic Enforcement's San Jose office;

Wade West, a media advisor who serves members of U.S. President George W. Bush's cabinet; and Ernst Aeschbach, a psychiatrist and psychotherapist in private practice in Switzerland, and an advisor to the Drug Free America Foundation.

Groups like the Compassion Club, which make pot available to the sick, have not been invited, however. " Why would we do that? " Bentall said. " The Compassion Club-that's not scientific evidence, that's opinion. It's a scam. There's not one bit of evidence that smoking marijuana is good medicine. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Not one bit of evidence?)
See
Chairman of the House of Lords Science and Technology Committee
Criticizes UK Government’s Rejection Of Report On Medical Marijuana
– 2 Articles With 2 of the Worst Prohibitionist Arguments

Bentall said she became interested in the drug issue through running the Ailanthus Achievement Centre on Commercial Drive, a performing arts group for inner-city students. The centre is located next door to a methadone clinic and kitty corner to the Compassion Club. " We see drug deals happening outside our window every day. We watch teenagers going in [the Compassion Club] by the line-up, " Bentall said.

" It's become this huge toxic social problem. "

" It's a question of the validity of the studies. Every leading expert around the world comes to the same conclusion. It's not that we have chosen people for a viewpoint. They all end up being against liberalization. All educated people on the topic end up being conservative. "

The IDEAS symposium is being presented on May 1 to 3 in partnership with the Drug Free America Foundation, Inc. and the Drug Prevention Network of the Americas.

Two Vancouver police officers, Toby Hinton and Al Arsenault-members of Odd Squad Productions, a group of Downtown Eastside officers who educate the public on drug issues-are listed as vice- presidents on IDEAS's board of directors.

Bentall said Hinton and Arsenault are participating as regular citizens, not as members of the Vancouver Police Department.
See
Marijuana Legalization, The Missing Pillar in Solving the Substance Abuse Problem in Vancouver and All of Canada. Analysis By Richard Cowan

(MarijuanaNews note: Finally, I cannot resist giving you one more example of how wonderfully tone-deaf these people are.

Their web site describes how they came up with this brilliant iDEA.

" On a rainy July day in Vancouver, over lunch at a fashionable bistro, four individuals were discussing their work, their challenges, their worries, and their hopes… "

From Mirriam-Webster:

bis·tro

Pronunciation: 'bEs-( " )trO, 'bis-
Function: noun
Etymology: French
1 : a small or unpretentious restaurant
2 a : a small bar or tavern b : NIGHTCLUB

They say that they decided to hold a conference on substance abuse at a bistro! Well, at least it was a fashionable bistro!

Canadian cannabis reform advocates and their anti-prohibitionist allies should not be lulled into complacency by the seeming ineptitude of these naïve tools of DEAland prohibitionists.

The fact that the Vancouver Courier was willing to run a libel of the highly regarded BC Compassion Society, without the courtesy of seeking a response, indicates that even in Canada, prohibitionist propaganda still finds a ready outlet.

Canadians need to mount an effective response to the iDEAs conference. The prohibitionists cannot and will not debate us, but we can easily prove that they are lying.

There is nothing new here, and the Internet is our medium and the reason that we will win.)
